items.heading: Most Advice Aimed At Fresh
items.text: Most advice aimed at fresh graduates answers a narrower question than the one they are actually asking. "How do I get hired" is a tactics problem: resumes, portals, referrals, interview prep. "How do I plan my career path" is a direction problem: what am I building toward, and what does the next few years need to add up to?

items.heading: Skipping Self
items.text: Skipping self-assessment and jumping straight to "which industry is booming" is the single most common reason a career plan collapses within a year. A direction built on market noise alone, without checking it against your own values, strengths, and interests, is a plan built for someone else's life.

items.heading: A Direction Is Not
items.text: A direction is not a map with every turn marked. It names where you are generally heading - a function, a problem space, an industry cluster - and leaves the exact route to be filled in as you learn more. Treat it as a compass reading, not a fixed itinerary.
